title: The State of AI Ethics
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not conduct a benchmark measurement but rather reviews and summarizes existing work. Its analysis related to faith/religion involves a qualitative discussion of diverse ethical and religious frameworks (Buddhism, Shinto, Ubuntu) as foundations for AI ethics, advocating for their inclusion alongside dominant Western ethical traditions.
findings: The paper finds that the AI ethics discourse is heavily dominated by Western ethical traditions and advocates for incorporating diverse perspectives from frameworks like Buddhism, Shinto, and Ubuntu to create a more globally representative approach to AI governance. It specifically notes the Buddhist view on privacy as a societal necessity and suggests that cultivating classical virtues, some with roots in world religions, within AI practitioners could be more effective than relying on abstract principles alone.
